newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul reports major Taleban offensive.
newsitem.headline: Kabul reports major Taleban offensive.

text.p: Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia launched a major offensive on Thursday afternoon on the government-held Azra district in Logar province, southeast of the capital Kabul, a government spokesman said.
Heavy fighting was raging after the Taleban launched the attack at about three p.m. (1030 gmt), said Amrullah, spokesman for main government commander Ahmad Shah Masood.

No details of the fighting were immediately available, but Amrullah told reporters that the Taleban appeared to be aiming to reach the strategic eastern town of Sarobi, which lies on the main highway linking the besieged capital with Pakistan.
No Taleban comment was immediately available.
The reported offensive comes after a government assault on Taleban positions southwest of Kabul on Monday, which had closed for a day the capital's supply route from the southwest.

A Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported last week that President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government had sent hundreds of troops to Sarobi, about 60 km (37 miles) east of Kabul, to defend it against possible Taleban attack.

Sarobi has long been a stronghold of Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party but Taleban advances against Hezb in neighbouring Paktia province last month prompted fears that it might be the Islamic militia's next target.
Amrullah said Taleban seemed to be trying to intensify fighting around Kabul to gain benefits before peace efforts by the international community could make much progress.
The Taleban, entrenched in hills south of Kabul for the past year, have sworn to oust Rabbani and impose strict Islamic rule throughout Afghanistan.
